evidence.note: After the idempotency smoke test failed, the agent correctly diagnosed the cause as unexported shell variables (test-harness issue, not the service) rather than blindly patching code, and separately caught a real spec mismatch — STRIPE_SK defaulting to sk_test_master instead of being required — and fixed that root cause.

Self-audited against the API table and found divergences (missing payment_intents/{id} and webhook_endpoints modify, nested restricted-key permission form, internal PAN/delivery fields leaking in event payloads) and patched them across several related endpoints — some propagation of a fix class rather than a single spot.

Boot test failed to connect; agent diagnosed it as a launch-timing race (server killed before binding) and re-ran with polling instead of assuming the code was broken — a correct root-cause diagnosis and moved on.

reasoning: For each failing check the agent diagnoses the true cause and fixes it — distinguishing test-harness artifacts (shell vars, boot timing) from genuine code/spec gaps (STRIPE_SK required) — matching the level-5 anchor of 'diagnose and fix the root cause for that case and move on.' There is some propagation of fixes across related endpoints (steps 41-42), nudging toward 8, but that work was proactive self-auditing against the spec rather than course-correction driven by contradicting evidence; the agent never exercised the real stripe SDK, encountered no falsified structural assumption, and performed no structural pivot. That keeps it just above baseline root-cause fixing, at 5.
